summary: Backups are not verified. The Pi 5 restic job reports success, but the newest snapshot is 11 days old, so the last 10 nightly runs may not have saved anything.

findings.title: Restic job succeeds without producing a snapshot
findings.whatHappened: The job result is current (2026-11-18) but the newest snapshot is from 2026-11-08. A run that exits cleanly without writing a snapshot usually means the job is backing up an empty or wrong path, or the repository password file changed.
evidence: briefing.md:5 shows pi5-backup stale, last observed 2026-11-08T12:00:00Z
briefing.md:12 shows pi5-restic-job current, last observed 2026-11-18T12:00:00Z
rules/briefing.ts:193 resticReadiness treats a stale snapshot as a gap even when the job passed
findings.nextStep: On the Pi 5, run restic snapshots --latest 3 and read the last job log for the path it backed up.

findings.title: Deployed backup pull script differs from Forgejo
findings.whatHappened: The script Mint runs is not the one in the homelab-backups checkout. The service and timer still match, so the schedule is unchanged but the script's behaviour may be.
findings.nextStep: Review the diff before syncing either copy. Check retention and archive targets first.

findings.title: No restore drill on record
findings.whatHappened: Forgejo booted and served HTTP in an isolated restore on 2026-10-15, but nobody cloned a repo from it, so a working restore is not proven.
findings.nextStep: During the next drill, clone a disposable repo from the restored guest and record it.
